newsitem.title: FRANCE: Danone sets novel ad package for World Cup.
newsitem.headline: Danone sets novel ad package for World Cup.

text.p: A novel package of advertising and sponsoring from French food group Danone is getting underway in France in the run-up to next year's World Cup football tournament, with the aim of tempting young football fans to taste Danone yoghurts and dairy deserts.
The food firm said on Friday a Danone product will be included in every "Happy Meal" from July 1 in McDonalds restaurants in France under an accord with the fast food chain.
The accord also makes Danone the exclusive supplier of chilled dairy products to McDonalds in France.
In another company-to-company advertising deal, stickers from Panini, a leader in sticker and sticker album collectables, will be inserted in Danone products' packaging.
Danone has also commissioned an advertising spot to run in 29 countries from Saatchi & Saatchi Advertising, which began showing in France and Poland at the end of last month.
It is the first time Danone has run an international advertising campaign.
The company is also sponsoring three football tournaments for children under 13, including one under its own name, which took place in Paris last weekend.
Tickets for this event were distributed in McDonalds restaurants in France as part of Danone's accord with McDonalds.
A Danone spokeswoman said the company would give no financial details of the advertising and sponsoring package.

Danone, picked last year as the official dairy products supplier for the World Cup, could not let an event of such scope pass as a promotion tool, said the company's marketing and corporate strategies director, Philippe Rambaud.
"Today Danone has the critical mass, both in terms of the group and of its products, to invest this heavily in sponsoring," he told daily newspaper Le Figaro this week.
"An event of this size gives a fantastic boost to notoriety and image," he said.
Up to now Danone's advertising has been product by product, while the company itself has not sought to project an image.
Its advertising spot, and a 500 square metres poster to be displayed on the heavily-used motorway to the South of France, use the name Danone as if it were the name of a team.
They show a small boy kicking a winning shot in a football stadium with the slogan: "Believe in your dreams. Play Danone."
